```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(csgjcr)
library(highcharter)
library(htmlwidgets)
library(reactable)

source("R/utils.R")
source("R/page-data.R")
source("R/local-map-data.R")

# htmlwidgets seeds its element IDs from this, so rerenders give identical HTML
set.seed(2019)

# params exists when Quarto renders; interactive runs use the YAML default
if (!exists("params")) {
  params <- list(state = "NY")
}

state <- csg_state_convert(params$state, from = "abbr", "name")
state_abbr_params <- params$state
state_name_text <- if_else(params$state == "DC", "the District of Columbia", state)
show_solved <- !state %in% states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz

### New York 2022 solve rates use NYPD clearance reports
nypd_note <- if (state == "New York") {
  paste(
    "", "In 2022, the New York City Police Department (NYPD) reported crimes to the FBI but no clearances.",
    "For that year, New York's solve rates for all violent crime, aggravated assault, and robbery use the",
    "average of the NYPD's four",
    "[quarterly clearance reports](https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/stats/reports-analysis/clearance.page){target=\"_parent\"}.",
    "In 2019 and 2020, those reports matched the NYPD's FBI clearance rates within half a percentage point",
    "for aggravated assault and robbery but not for homicide and rape. New York's 2022 homicide and rape",
    "solve rates are therefore omitted."
  )
} else {
  ""
}

srs_state_new <- read_srs_state()
latest_year <- max(srs_state_new$year)
first_year <- latest_year - 10

srs_state <- violent_by_offense(srs_state_new, first_year, state)
srs_by_cat_state <- violent_totals(srs_state_new, first_year, state)
srs_by_cat_us <- violent_totals(srs_state_new, first_year)
srs_us <- violent_by_offense(srs_state_new, first_year)

### the US solve rate leaves out the excluded states but applies to US reported counts
srs_by_cat_us_solve <- us_solve_trend(srs_state_new, first_year)
solve_coverage <- read_solve_coverage()
state_solve_coverage <- solve_coverage$coverage[solve_coverage$state_name == state]
us_solve_coverage <- solve_coverage$coverage[solve_coverage$state_name == "United States"]

### county map and agency tables come from R/01-prep-agency-county-data.R
srs_solved_by_county_to_map <- read_rds("data/county_map.rds") |>
  filter(state_abbr == state_abbr_params)

agency_table_all <- read_rds("data/agency_table.rds")

### years are read before filtering so states with no agency rows still get them
### the agency base year comes from the data built by R/01-prep-agency-county-data.R
agency_year <- agency_table_all$agency_year[1]
agency_base_year <- agency_table_all$base_year[1]

if (agency_base_year != base_year) {
  stop("The agency tables use base year ", agency_base_year, " but R/page-data.R sets ",
       base_year, ". Rerun R/01-prep-agency-county-data.R.", call. = FALSE)
}

### state total rows in the agency tables match the charts and text only in the same year
if (agency_year != latest_year) {
  stop("The agency tables use ", agency_year, " but the state estimates end in ",
       latest_year, ". Update the agency data and rerun R/01-prep-agency-county-data.R.",
       call. = FALSE)
}

srs_solved_by_agency_to_table <- agency_table_all |>
  filter(state_abbr == state_abbr_params)

srs_solved_by_agency_and_offense_to_table <- read_rds("data/agency_offense_table.rds") |>
  filter(state_abbr == state_abbr_params)

### pages without solve-rate data drop "and solve rates" from the title
doc_title <- if_else(
  show_solved,
  paste(state, "data on violent crime and solve rates"),
  paste(state, "data on violent crime")
)

### shown in place of each solve-rate section on pages without solve-rate data
no_solve_data_text <- paste(state_name_text, "did not report enough data on solved crime to the FBI to make reliable estimates.")
```

         state_abbr = geo_abbr)

#| output: asis

### show-solved shows the solve-rate sections; when it's false or missing,
### the pages show no_solve_data_text instead
### the flag is written here because when-meta needs a YAML boolean, and an
### inline-R value in the title block arrives as a string
### the title stays in that block because a title written from a chunk
### doesn't reach the page's <title>
cat("---\nshow-solved: ", tolower(show_solved), "\n---\n", sep = "")

### text and the agency tables' state total rows share these values, comparing

state_total <- total_rate_benchmark(srs_by_cat_state, base_year, latest_year)
us_total <- total_rate_benchmark(srs_by_cat_us, base_year, latest_year, solves = srs_by_cat_us_solve)

change_text_crime <- change_phrase(state_total$rate_change / 100)
us_state_rate_text_crime <- change_phrase((state_total$rate_100k - us_total$rate_100k) / us_total$rate_100k)

### pages without solve-rate data hide the solve text, and their solve rates may be missing

```{r }
# ==============================================================================
# Crime Without Consequence, state pages: two accessible highcharter charts
#   Chart 1 (hc_reported_solved): Violent crime reported, solved, and unsolved
#   Chart 2 (hc_backlog): Backlog of unsolved violent crime, stacked by offense
# Everything is driven by the data passed in, so the same code runs for any state.
# ==============================================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PREP DATA FOR FIRST SECTION
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
crime_data <- srs_by_cat_state |>
  ### filter on years in handout
  filter(year%in%c(2020:2025)) |>
  mutate(
    cumulative_incidents_unsolved = cumsum(incidents_unsolved)     # backlog added since 2020
  )

# hc_setup() shows each point's `tooltip` column, so build that text per chart.
# Chart 1: one tooltip per year listing all three values, plus the running
# total of unsolved crimes since 2020 as the last row.
trend_data <- crime_data |>
  mutate(tooltip = paste0(
    "<b>", year, "</b><br>",
    "Violent crimes reported: ", comma(incidents_reported, 1), "<br>",
    "Violent crimes solved: ", comma(incidents_solved, 1), "<br>",
    "Violent crimes unsolved: ", comma(incidents_unsolved, 1), "<br>",
    "<b>Total unsolved since 2020: ", comma(cumulative_incidents_unsolved, 1), "</b>"
  ))

# Chart 2: backlog tooltip for the total line (dots and numbers).
backlog_data <- crime_data |>
  mutate(tooltip = paste0(
    "<b>", year, "</b><br>",
    "Unsolved crimes added since 2020: ", comma(cumulative_incidents_unsolved, 1), "<br>",
    "Unsolved this year: ", comma(incidents_unsolved, 1)
  ))

```

```{r }
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# COLORS (from the handout) AND SMALL HELPERS
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
col_navy <- "#001E35"   # reported line, backlog total line
col_blue <- "#005DA6"   # solved line, callout outline
col_gap  <- "#CCE9FF"   # shaded "unsolved" gap

# Offense colors, matching the microsite's 50-state crime data page. The order
# is the stack order, bottom to top (largest slice at the bottom).
offense_order <- c("Aggravated assault", "Robbery", "Rape", "Homicide")
offense_fills <- c(
  "Aggravated assault" = "#005DA6",
  "Robbery"            = "#7397B0",
  "Rape"               = "#2DEBC3",
  "Homicide"           = "#001E35"
)

# Compact number formatter used inside the JS below. Scales itself to the data:
#   1,313,000 -> "1.31M"   25,300 -> "25.3K"   563,000 -> "563K"   840 -> "840"
# trim = TRUE drops trailing zeros (axis ticks: "1M", "1.5M");
# dm = decimals for millions.
crime_js_fmt <- "var fmt = function(v, trim, dm) {
    var a = Math.abs(v); dm = (dm === undefined) ? 2 : dm;
    var out;
    if (a >= 1e6) { out = (v / 1e6).toFixed(dm); return (trim ? String(+out) : out) + 'M'; }
    if (a >= 1e3) { out = (v / 1e3).toFixed(a >= 1e5 ? 0 : 1); return (trim ? String(+out) : out) + 'K'; }
    return String(Math.round(v));
  };"

# Axis labels. plus = TRUE gives +1M, +2M ... and a blue "?" at the baseline
# (the handout's way of saying the pre-2020 backlog is unknown).
crime_js_axis_label <- function(plus = FALSE) {
  JS(paste0(
    "function() { ", crime_js_fmt, "
      var v = this.value;
      if (v === 0) return ",
    if (plus) "'<span style=\"color:#005DA6;font-weight:900\">?</span>'" else "'0'", ";
      return ", if (plus) "'+' + fmt(v, true)" else "fmt(v, true)", ";
    }"
  ))
}

# Value labels on the lines: 1.31M, 563K
crime_js_point_label <- JS(paste0(
  "function() { ", crime_js_fmt, " return fmt(this.y, false); }"
))

# Direct line label: the series name on the LAST point only
crime_js_end_label <- JS("function() {
  return this.point.index === this.series.data.length - 1 ? this.series.name : null;
}")

# Last-point label on the backlog chart: +4.3M (null for every other point)
crime_js_backlog_label <- JS(paste0(
  "function() { ", crime_js_fmt, "
    return this.point.index === this.series.data.length - 1
      ? '+' + fmt(this.y, true, 1) : null;
  }"
))

# "Not starting at zero" note: borderless text plus an angled dotted line,
# drawn in a render event (the same way the site attaches end_labels).
#   note_frac  box CENTER height as a fraction of the y-axis range (0.45 puts it
#              at +2.25M on a 0-5M axis; it follows whatever the axis becomes)
#   max_width  widest the box may get, in px (also capped at 30% of the plot)
#   end_frac   how far above the baseline the dotted line ends (fraction of the
#              plot height)
# The box height is measured at render time, so the line always starts at the
# bottom of the box. It is redrawn on every render (resize, print).
crime_js_note_line <- function(note_frac = 0.45, max_width = 170, end_frac = 0.09) {
  JS(paste0("function() {
  var chart = this, accent = '#005DA6';
  var axis = chart.yAxis[0];
  var noteValue = axis.min + ", note_frac, " * (axis.max - axis.min);
  if (chart.noteGroup) chart.noteGroup.destroy();
  var g = chart.renderer.g('not-starting-at-zero-note').attr({ zIndex: 7 }).add();
  chart.noteGroup = g;
  var plotH = chart.plotHeight;
  var xEnd = chart.plotLeft + 2;                           // line ends at the y-axis
  var yEnd = chart.plotTop + plotH - ", end_frac, " * plotH; // just above the baseline
  var yCenter = axis.toPixels(noteValue);

  // Borderless text (no fill, no outline). SVG label (not HTML), so tooltips draw on top.
  var html = '<span style=\"color:' + accent + ';font-weight:700\">Not starting at zero:</span> ' +
             'added on top of unsolved crimes from before the first year shown';
  var note = chart.renderer.label(html, xEnd + 6, 0, 'rect')
    .css({ width: Math.min(", max_width, ", chart.plotWidth * 0.3) + 'px',
           color: '#000000', fontSize: '13px' })
    .attr({ fill: 'none', padding: 8, zIndex: 8 })
    .add(g);
  var box = note.getBBox();
  note.attr({ y: yCenter - box.height / 2 });

  // Dotted line from the bottom of the box down-left to the axis
  var xTop = xEnd + 6 + 16, yTop = yCenter + box.height / 2;
  chart.renderer.path(['M', xTop, yTop, 'L', xEnd, yEnd])
    .attr({ stroke: accent, 'stroke-width': 1.5, 'stroke-dasharray': '3,3',
            fill: 'none', zIndex: 7 })
    .add(g);

  // Remember the box so tooltips can steer around it
  chart.noteBox = { left: xEnd + 6, right: xEnd + 6 + box.width,
                    top: yCenter - box.height / 2, bottom: yCenter + box.height / 2 };
}"))
}

# Tooltip position: beside the point (flipping left near the right edge),
# centered on it vertically and kept inside the plot. If that would cover the
# note box, drop just below the box so both stay legible.
crime_js_tooltip_position <- JS("function(labelWidth, labelHeight, point) {
  var chart = this.chart, gap = 12;
  var plotBottom = chart.plotTop + chart.plotHeight;
  var px = chart.plotLeft + point.plotX, py = chart.plotTop + point.plotY;
  var x = px + gap;
  if (x + labelWidth > chart.plotLeft + chart.plotWidth) x = px - labelWidth - gap;
  var y = Math.min(Math.max(py - labelHeight / 2, chart.plotTop), plotBottom - labelHeight);
  var nb = chart.noteBox;
  if (nb && x < nb.right && x + labelWidth > nb.left &&
      y < nb.bottom && y + labelHeight > nb.top) {
    y = Math.min(nb.bottom + 6, plotBottom - labelHeight);
  }
  return { x: x, y: y };
}")

# Sets only the long description for screen readers, so the accessibility
# options hc_setup() already set are kept.
crime_hc_describe <- function(chart, text) {
  chart$x$hc_opts$accessibility$description <- text
  chart
}

# Source line shared by both charts
crime_caption <- "FBI UCR Program, state crime estimates and clearances"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MICROSITE LOOK (same as the national page)
# Libre Franklin type, black 800-weight headings, blue-gray secondary text,
# light blue-gray borders, 8px rounded cards. Merged on top of the site theme
# (hc_theme_jc) and applied to these two charts after hc_setup(). These
# definitions are identical on the national page, so you could move them into
# the functions file and delete the copies.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ONE plain font name (no commas or quotes): highcharter turns it into a Google
# Fonts link, and a font stack breaks rendering.
microsite_font <- "Libre Franklin"
microsite_text <- "#4B5D6E"   # subtitles, captions, axis labels (about 7:1 on white)
microsite_line <- "#D5E0EA"   # gridlines, axis lines, card border

hc_theme_microsite <- hc_theme_merge(
  hc_theme_jc,
  hc_theme(
    # Delete borderColor/borderWidth/borderRadius for a borderless chart
    chart = list(
      style = list(fontFamily = microsite_font),
      borderColor = microsite_line, borderWidth = 1, borderRadius = 8
    ),
    title = list(style = list(fontFamily = microsite_font, color = "#000000",
                              fontSize = "22px", fontWeight = "800")),
    subtitle = list(style = list(fontFamily = microsite_font, color = microsite_text,
                                 fontSize = "15px")),
    caption = list(style = list(fontFamily = microsite_font, color = microsite_text,
                                fontSize = "13px")),
    xAxis = list(lineColor = microsite_line, tickColor = microsite_line,
                 labels = list(style = list(color = microsite_text, fontSize = "13px"))),
    yAxis = list(gridLineColor = microsite_line,
                 labels = list(style = list(color = microsite_text, fontSize = "13px"))),
    legend = list(itemStyle = list(color = "#000000", fontSize = "14px", fontWeight = "600")),
    tooltip = list(backgroundColor = "#FFFFFF", borderColor = microsite_line,
                   borderRadius = 8,
                   style = list(color = "#000000", fontSize = "14px"))
  )
)
```

```{r }
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. THE CHART BUILDER
#   data            one row per year: year, incidents_reported, incidents_solved,
#                   incidents_unsolved (the state's totals)
#   offense_data    one row per offense and year: group (the offense), year,
#                   incidents_reported, incidents_solved (the state's offense-
#                   level data, used for the stacked slices in chart 2)
#   place           how the place reads in titles, e.g. "Ohio"
#   y_expansion     headroom above the largest value, as a share of it
#                   (room for the value labels); passed to chart_bounds()
#   x_pad           blank space (in years) before the first and after the last
#                   year; leaves room for the end labels and the note line
#   line_label_margin  right margin (px) reserved for the "Reported"/"Solved"
#                   end labels
#   note_frac, note_max_width, note_end_frac   see crime_js_note_line()
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
crime_trend_charts <- function(data, offense_data, place, caption = crime_caption,
                               y_expansion = 0.2, x_pad = 0.4,
                               line_label_margin = 70,
                               note_frac = 0.45, note_max_width = 170,
                               note_end_frac = 0.09) {

  # ---- 3a. Data prep: everything below is computed from the data -------------
  data <- data |>
    arrange(year) |>
    mutate(
      cumulative_incidents_unsolved = cumsum(incidents_unsolved)
    )
  years      <- data$year
  year_range <- paste0(min(years), "–", max(years))   # e.g. 2020-2025

  # hc_setup() shows each point's `tooltip` column
  trend_data <- data |>
    mutate(tooltip = paste0(
      "<b>", year, "</b><br>",
      "Violent crimes reported: ", comma(incidents_reported, 1), "<br>",
      "Violent crimes solved: ", comma(incidents_solved, 1), "<br>",
      "Violent crimes unsolved: ", comma(incidents_unsolved, 1), "<br>",
      "<b>Total unsolved since ", min(years), ": ", comma(cumulative_incidents_unsolved, 1), "</b>"
    ))
  backlog_data <- data |>
    mutate(tooltip = paste0(
      "<b>", year, "</b><br>",
      "Unsolved crimes added since ", min(years), ": ", comma(cumulative_incidents_unsolved, 1), "<br>",
      "Unsolved this year: ", comma(incidents_unsolved, 1)
    ))

  # One stacked slice per offense. complete() adds a zero row for any offense
  # or year a state has no data for, so every slice has a point in every year.
  # (Missing counts are treated as zero for the slices only.)
  offense_backlog <- offense_data |>
    filter(year %in% years, group %in% offense_order) |>
    mutate(
      group = factor(group, levels = offense_order),
      incidents_unsolved = incidents_reported - incidents_solved
    ) |>
    tidyr::complete(
      group, year = years,
      fill = list(incidents_reported = 0, incidents_solved = 0, incidents_unsolved = 0)
    ) |>
    arrange(group, year) |>
    group_by(group) |>
    mutate(cumulative_incidents_unsolved = cumsum(coalesce(incidents_unsolved, 0))) |>
    ungroup() |>
    left_join(
      data |> select(year, total_cumulative = cumulative_incidents_unsolved),
      by = "year"
    )

  # The slices should add up to the total line; warn if they are more than 0.5%
  # apart (small gaps are invisible on the chart)
  stack_check <- offense_backlog |>
    summarize(slices = sum(cumulative_incidents_unsolved), .by = c(year, total_cumulative))
  if (any(abs(stack_check$slices - stack_check$total_cumulative) /
            pmax(stack_check$total_cumulative, 1) > 0.005, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    warning("Offense slices do not add up to the total backlog for ", place,
            "; check the offense-level data", call. = FALSE)
  }

  # ---- 3b. Axis limits from the data (same idea as the site's trend_chart()) --
  # Including 0 in the values anchors the baseline at zero; chart_bounds()
  # then adds `y_expansion` headroom above the largest value. endOnTick = FALSE
  # lets Highcharts choose tick spacing for whatever the range turns out to be.
  trend_bounds   <- chart_bounds(c(0, data$incidents_reported), expansion = y_expansion, floor = 0)
  backlog_bounds <- chart_bounds(c(0, data$cumulative_incidents_unsolved),
                                 expansion = y_expansion, floor = 0)

  # Whole-year ticks, padded on both sides
  x_min <- min(years) - x_pad
  x_max <- max(years) + x_pad

  # ---- 3c. Where to put the "Unsolved" label ---------------------------------
  # Centered horizontally on the x-axis (the middle of the years shown), and
  # vertically halfway between the two lines at that point. The lines are
  # straight between years, so the halfway height at the center is
  # interpolated from the yearly midpoints.
  x_center <- mean(range(years))
  gap_label_data <- tibble(
    year = x_center,
    mid  = approx(years, (data$incidents_reported + data$incidents_solved) / 2,
                  xout = x_center)$y
  )

  # ---- 3d. Screen-reader descriptions built from the numbers -----------------
  desc_trend <- paste0(
    "Line chart with a shaded gap, ", min(years), " to ", max(years), ", for ", place,
    ". Violent crimes reported went from ", comma(first(data$incidents_reported), 1), " in ",
    min(years), " to ", comma(last(data$incidents_reported), 1), " in ", max(years),
    ". Violent crimes solved ranged between ", comma(min(data$incidents_solved), 1), " and ",
    comma(max(data$incidents_solved), 1), " each year. The shaded area between the two lines ",
    "is the number left unsolved each year: ", comma(first(data$incidents_unsolved), 1), " in ",
    min(years), " and ", comma(last(data$incidents_unsolved), 1), " in ", max(years),
    ". In total, ", comma(last(data$cumulative_incidents_unsolved), 1),
    " violent crimes went unsolved from ", min(years), " through ", max(years), "."
  )

  # Each offense's share of the backlog in the last year, for the description
  # (e.g., "aggravated assault 65 percent")
  last_totals <- offense_backlog |> filter(year == max(year))
  offense_share_text <- if (sum(last_totals$cumulative_incidents_unsolved) > 0) {
    last_totals |>
      mutate(share = cumulative_incidents_unsolved / sum(cumulative_incidents_unsolved)) |>
      arrange(desc(share)) |>
      mutate(text = paste0(tolower(as.character(group)), " ",
                           percent(share, 1, suffix = " percent"))) |>
      pull(text) |>
      knitr::combine_words()
  } else {
    "not available"
  }
  desc_backlog <- paste0(
    "Stacked area chart, ", min(years), " to ", max(years), ", for ", place,
    ". The backlog of unsolved violent crimes added since ", min(years),
    " grows every year, from ", comma(first(data$cumulative_incidents_unsolved), 1),
    " at the end of ", min(years), " to ", comma(last(data$cumulative_incidents_unsolved), 1),
    " by the end of ", max(years), ". The area is divided by offense. By the end of ",
    max(years), ", the backlog is ", offense_share_text,
    ". The chart does not start from zero in real terms: ",
    "these crimes are added on top of an unknown number of unsolved crimes from before ",
    min(years), "."
  )

  # ---- 3e. CHART 1: reported, solved, unsolved -------------------------------
  # The shaded gap is two stacked area series: an invisible base that follows
  # the solved line, with the unsolved amount stacked on top in light blue.
  trend <- hchart(
    trend_data, "area", hcaes(year, incidents_solved),
    name = "Solved (base of gap)", color = "transparent", fillOpacity = 0,
    lineWidth = 0, stacking = "normal", marker = list(enabled = FALSE),
    enableMouseTracking = FALSE, zIndex = 0,
    accessibility = list(enabled = FALSE)
  ) |>
    hc_add_series(
      trend_data, "area", hcaes(year, incidents_unsolved),
      name = "Unsolved", color = col_gap, fillOpacity = 1, lineWidth = 0,
      stacking = "normal", marker = list(enabled = FALSE),
      enableMouseTracking = FALSE, zIndex = 0,
      accessibility = list(
        description = "Shaded area showing violent crimes left unsolved each year.",
        point = list(valueDescriptionFormat =
          "year: {point.x:.0f}, violent crimes unsolved: {point.y:,.0f}")
      )
    ) |>
    # Invisible helper that carries the "Unsolved" label inside the gap
    hc_add_series(
      gap_label_data, "line", hcaes(year, mid),
      name = "Unsolved (label)", lineWidth = 0, marker = list(enabled = FALSE),
      enableMouseTracking = FALSE, zIndex = 1,
      dataLabels = list(enabled = TRUE, format = "Unsolved", align = "center",
                        verticalAlign = "middle", y = 0, allowOverlap = TRUE,
                        style = list(color = "#000000", fontSize = "15px",
                                     fontWeight = "800", textOutline = "none")),
      accessibility = list(enabled = FALSE)
    ) |>
    # Reported: solid navy line; value labels above, name label at the line end
    hc_add_series(
      trend_data, "line", hcaes(year, incidents_reported),
      name = "Reported", color = col_navy, lineWidth = 3, zIndex = 2,
      marker = list(symbol = "circle", radius = 4, lineColor = "#FFFFFF", lineWidth = 1.5),
      dataLabels = list(
        list(enabled = TRUE, formatter = crime_js_point_label,
             verticalAlign = "bottom", y = -6,
             style = list(color = col_navy, fontSize = "13px",
                          fontWeight = "400", textOutline = "none")),
        list(enabled = TRUE, formatter = crime_js_end_label,
             align = "left", verticalAlign = "middle", x = 10, y = 0,
             crop = FALSE, overflow = "allow", allowOverlap = TRUE,
             style = list(color = col_navy, fontSize = "15px",
                          fontWeight = "800", textOutline = "none"))
      ),
      accessibility = list(
        description = "Violent crimes reported each year.",
        point = list(valueDescriptionFormat =
          "year: {point.x:.0f}, violent crimes reported: {point.y:,.0f}")
      )
    ) |>
    # Solved: dashed blue line, diamond markers (differs by more than color)
    hc_add_series(
      trend_data, "line", hcaes(year, incidents_solved),
      name = "Solved", color = col_blue, lineWidth = 3, dashStyle = "ShortDash",
      zIndex = 2,
      marker = list(symbol = "diamond", radius = 5, lineColor = "#FFFFFF", lineWidth = 1.5),
      dataLabels = list(
        list(enabled = TRUE, formatter = crime_js_point_label,
             verticalAlign = "top", y = 8,
             style = list(color = col_blue, fontSize = "13px",
                          fontWeight = "400", textOutline = "none")),
        list(enabled = TRUE, formatter = crime_js_end_label,
             align = "left", verticalAlign = "middle", x = 10, y = 0,
             crop = FALSE, overflow = "allow", allowOverlap = TRUE,
             style = list(color = col_blue, fontSize = "15px",
                          fontWeight = "800", textOutline = "none"))
      ),
      accessibility = list(
        description = "Violent crimes solved each year.",
        point = list(valueDescriptionFormat =
          "year: {point.x:.0f}, violent crimes solved: {point.y:,.0f}")
      )
    ) |>
    hc_title(text = paste0("Violent crime reported, solved, and unsolved in ",
                           place)) |>
    hc_caption(text = caption) |>
    hc_legend(enabled = FALSE) |>
    hc_setup() |>
    # Microsite look (fonts, heading colors, borders); must come after hc_setup()
    hc_add_theme(hc_theme_microsite) |>
    # Chart-specific settings go AFTER hc_setup() so they merge into its defaults
    hc_xAxis(tickPositions = years, min = x_min, max = x_max) |>
    hc_yAxis(min = trend_bounds[1], max = trend_bounds[2], endOnTick = FALSE,
             reversedStacks = FALSE,            # base series sits at the bottom
             labels = list(formatter = crime_js_axis_label(plus = FALSE))) |>
    hc_chart(marginRight = line_label_margin) |>
    crime_hc_describe(desc_trend)

  # ---- 3f. CHART 2: cumulative backlog, stacked by offense -------------------
  # Four stacked area slices (one per offense) add up to the total backlog. A
  # line on top keeps the black dots and the "+4.3M"-style total label.
  backlog <- highchart()

  for (g in offense_order) {
    backlog <- backlog |>
      hc_add_series(
        filter(offense_backlog, group == g), "area",
        hcaes(year, cumulative_incidents_unsolved),
        name = g, color = offense_fills[[g]], fillOpacity = 1,
        lineWidth = 1, lineColor = "#FFFFFF", stacking = "normal",
        marker = list(enabled = FALSE, states = list(hover = list(enabled = FALSE))),
        # The slices have no hover tooltip; the total line's tooltip is the only
        # one. Keyboard and screen-reader users still get each slice's numbers
        # from the accessibility descriptions.
        enableMouseTracking = FALSE,
        zIndex = 1,
        accessibility = list(
          description = paste0("Unsolved ", tolower(g), " cases added to the backlog since ",
                               min(years), "."),
          point = list(valueDescriptionFormat = paste0(
            "{point.series.name}, year: {point.x:.0f}, ",
            "unsolved added since ", min(years), ": {point.y:,.0f}"))
        )
      )
  }

  backlog <- backlog |>
    # Total line on top of the stack: black dots and the last-point label. Left
    # out of the legend because the slices already add up to it.
    hc_add_series(
      backlog_data, "line", hcaes(year, cumulative_incidents_unsolved),
      name = paste0("Total backlog added since ", min(years)),
      color = col_navy, lineWidth = 2, zIndex = 3, showInLegend = FALSE,
      # Black dots with a white edge, so they can't be mistaken for an offense color
      marker = list(enabled = TRUE, symbol = "circle", radius = 4,
                    fillColor = "#000000", lineColor = "#FFFFFF", lineWidth = 1.5),
      dataLabels = list(enabled = TRUE, align = "right", verticalAlign = "bottom", y = -8,
                        formatter = crime_js_backlog_label,
                        style = list(color = "#000000", fontSize = "13px",
                                     fontWeight = "800", textOutline = "none")),
      accessibility = list(
        description = paste0("Total unsolved violent crimes added to the backlog since ",
                             min(years), ", all offenses combined."),
        point = list(valueDescriptionFormat = paste0(
          "year: {point.x:.0f}, total unsolved violent crimes added since ", min(years),
          ": {point.y:,.0f}"))
      )
    ) |>
    hc_title(text = paste0("Backlog of unsolved violent crime in ", place)) |>
    hc_subtitle(text = paste0("Unsolved violent crimes added since ", min(years), ", by offense")) |>
    hc_caption(text = caption) |>
    # Legend names the four slices (clicking is already disabled by hc_setup())
    hc_legend(enabled = TRUE, reversed = FALSE) |>
    hc_setup() |>
    # Microsite look (fonts, heading colors, borders); must come after hc_setup()
    hc_add_theme(hc_theme_microsite) |>
    hc_xAxis(tickPositions = years, min = min(years) - x_pad * 0.75,
             max = max(years) + x_pad * 0.75) |>
    # reversedStacks = FALSE puts the first offense (aggravated assault) at the bottom
    hc_yAxis(min = backlog_bounds[1], max = backlog_bounds[2], endOnTick = FALSE,
             reversedStacks = FALSE,
             labels = list(formatter = crime_js_axis_label(plus = TRUE), useHTML = TRUE)) |>
    # Note box + dotted line, added after hc_setup() the way the site adds end_labels
    hc_chart(events = list(render = crime_js_note_line(note_frac, note_max_width,
                                                        note_end_frac))) |>
    # Keep tooltips from covering the note
    hc_tooltip(positioner = crime_js_tooltip_position) |>
    crime_hc_describe(desc_backlog)

  list(trend = trend, backlog = backlog)
}
```

## The backlog of unsolved violent crime is adding up.

state_charts <- crime_trend_charts(
  crime_data, offense_data = srs_state, place = paste0(state_name_text)
)

hc_reported_solved
